   131→def _migrate_deferred_to_skipped(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   132→    deferred: list[str] = plan["deferred"]
   133→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   134→    if not deferred:
   135→        return
   136→
   137→    now = utc_now()
   138→    for fid in list(deferred):
   139→        if fid in skipped:
   140→            continue
   141→        skipped[fid] = {
   142→            "finding_id": fid,
   143→            "kind": "temporary",
   144→            "reason": None,
   145→            "note": None,
   146→            "attestation": None,
   147→            "created_at": now,
   148→            "review_after": None,
   149→            "skipped_at_scan": 0,
   150→        }
   151→    deferred.clear()
   152→
   153→
   154→def _normalize_cluster_defaults(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   155→    for cluster in plan["clusters"].values():
   156→        if not isinstance(cluster, dict):
   157→            continue
   158→        if not isinstance(cluster.get("finding_ids"), list):
   159→            cluster["finding_ids"] = []
   160→        cluster.setdefault("auto", False)
   161→        cluster.setdefault("cluster_key", "")
   162→        cluster.setdefault("action", None)
   163→        cluster.setdefault("user_modified", False)
   164→
   165→
   166→def _migrate_epics_to_clusters(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   167→    """Migrate v3 top-level ``epics`` dict into ``clusters`` (v4 unification)."""
   168→    epics = plan.pop("epics", None)
   169→    if not isinstance(epics, dict) or not epics:
   170→        return
   171→    clusters = plan["clusters"]
   172→    now = utc_now()
   173→    for name, epic in epics.items():
   174→        if not isinstance(epic, dict):
   175→            continue
   176→        if name in clusters:
   177→            continue  # don't overwrite existing cluster
   178→        clusters[name] = {
   179→            "name": name,
   180→            "description": epic.get("thesis", ""),
   181→            "finding_ids": epic.get("finding_ids", []),
   182→            "auto": True,
   183→            "cluster_key": f"epic::{name}",
   184→            "action": f"desloppify plan focus {name}",
   185→            "user_modified": False,
   186→            "created_at": epic.get("created_at", now),
   187→            "updated_at": epic.get("updated_at", now),
   188→            # Epic-specific fields
   189→            "thesis": epic.get("thesis", ""),
   190→            "direction": epic.get("direction", "simplify"),
   191→            "root_cause": epic.get("root_cause", ""),
   192→            "supersedes": epic.get("supersedes", []),
   193→            "dismissed": epic.get("dismissed", []),
   194→            "agent_safe": epic.get("agent_safe", False),
   195→            "dependency_order": epic.get("dependency_order", 999),
   196→            "action_steps": epic.get("action_steps", []),
   197→            "source_clusters": epic.get("source_clusters", []),
   198→            "status": epic.get("status", "pending"),
   199→            "synthesis_version": epic.get("synthesis_version", 0),
   200→        }
   201→
   202→
   203→def ensure_plan_defaults(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   204→    """Normalize a loaded plan to ensure all keys exist.
   205→
   206→    Handles migration from v1 (deferred list) to v2 (skipped dict),
   207→    and v3 (top-level epics) to v4 (epics unified into clusters).
   208→    """
   209→    defaults = empty_plan()
   210→    for key, value in defaults.items():
   211→        plan.setdefault(key, value)
   212→
   213→    _ensure_container_types(plan)
   214→    _migrate_deferred_to_skipped(plan)
   215→    _migrate_epics_to_clusters(plan)
   216→    _normalize_cluster_defaults(plan)
   217→
   218→
   219→def synthesis_clusters(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Cluster]:
   220→    """Return clusters whose name starts with ``EPIC_PREFIX``."""
   221→    return {
   222→        name: cluster
   223→        for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items()
   224→        if name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX)
   225→    }
   226→
   227→
   228→def validate_plan(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   229→    """Raise ValueError when plan invariants are violated."""
   230→    if not isinstance(plan.get("version"), int):
   231→        raise ValueError("plan.version must be an int")
   232→    if not isinstance(plan.get("queue_order"), list):
   233→        raise ValueError("plan.queue_order must be a list")
   234→
   235→    # No ID should appear in both queue_order and skipped
   236→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   237→    overlap = set(plan["queue_order"]) & skipped_ids
   238→    if overlap:
   239→        raise ValueError(
   240→            f"IDs cannot appear in both queue_order and skipped: {sorted(overlap)}"
   241→        )
   242→
   243→    # Validate skip entry kinds
   244→    for fid, entry in plan.get("skipped", {}).items():
   245→        kind = entry.get("kind")
   246→        if kind not in VALID_SKIP_KINDS:
   247→            raise ValueError(
   248→                f"Invalid skip kind {kind!r} for {fid}; must be one of {sorted(VALID_SKIP_KINDS)}"
   249→            )
   250→
   251→
   252→__all__ = [
   253→    "EPIC_PREFIX",
   254→    "ExecutionLogEntry",
   255→    "PLAN_VERSION",
   256→    "Cluster",
   257→    "ItemOverride",
   258→    "PlanModel",
   259→    "SkipEntry",
   260→    "SupersededEntry",
   261→    "VALID_EPIC_DIRECTIONS",
   262→    "VALID_SKIP_KINDS",
   263→    "empty_plan",
   264→    "ensure_plan_defaults",
   265→    "synthesis_clusters",
   266→    "validate_plan",
   267→]

   229→    payload: dict[str, object] = {

   235→    }
   236→    if extra:

   244→def _apply_completion(args: argparse.Namespace, plan: dict, strategy: str) -> None:
   245→    """Shared completion logic: update meta, remove synthesis::pending, save."""

   328→    for fid, finding in sorted(resolved.items())[:10]:

   332→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "")

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import json
     6→import logging

     8→import sys
     9→from pathlib import Path

    11→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import safe_write_text
    12→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import (
    13→    PLAN_VERSION,
    14→    PlanModel,
    15→    empty_plan,
    16→    ensure_plan_defaults,
    17→    validate_plan,
    18→)
    19→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import STATE_DIR, json_default
    20→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import utc_now
    21→
    22→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    23→
    24→PLAN_FILE = STATE_DIR / "plan.json"
    25→
    26→
    27→def load_plan(path: Path | None = None) -> PlanModel:
    28→    """Load plan from disk, or return empty plan on missing/corruption."""
    29→    plan_path = path or PLAN_FILE
    30→    if not plan_path.exists():
    31→        return empty_plan()
    32→
    33→    try:
    34→        data = json.loads(plan_path.read_text())
    35→    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) as ex:
    36→        # Try backup before giving up
    37→        backup = plan_path.with_suffix(".json.bak")
    38→        if backup.exists():
    39→            try:
    40→                data = json.loads(backup.read_text())
    41→                logger.warning("Plan file corrupted (%s), loaded from backup.", ex)
    42→                print(f"  Warning: Plan file corrupted ({ex}), loaded from backup.", file=sys.stderr)
    43→                # Fall through to validation below
    44→            except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) as backup_ex:
    45→                logger.warning("Plan file and backup both corrupted: %s / %s", ex, backup_ex)
    46→                print(f"  Warning: Plan file corrupted ({ex}). Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    47→                return empty_plan()
    48→        else:
    49→            logger.warning("Plan file corrupted (%s). Starting fresh.", ex)
    50→            print(f"  Warning: Plan file corrupted ({ex}). Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    51→            return empty_plan()
    52→
    53→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    54→        logger.warning("Plan file root is not a JSON object. Starting fresh.")
    55→        print("  Warning: Plan file root must be a JSON object. Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    56→        return empty_plan()
    57→
    58→    version = data.get("version", 1)
    59→    if version > PLAN_VERSION:
    60→        logger.warning("Plan file version %d > supported %d.", version, PLAN_VERSION)
    61→        print(
    62→            f"  Warning: Plan file version {version} is newer than supported "
    63→            f"({PLAN_VERSION}). Some features may not work correctly.",
    64→            file=sys.stderr,
    65→        )
    66→
    67→    ensure_plan_defaults(data)
    68→    try:
    69→        validate_plan(data)
    70→    except ValueError as ex:
    71→        logger.warning("Plan invariants invalid (%s). Starting fresh.", ex)
    72→        print(f"  Warning: Plan invariants invalid ({ex}). Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    73→        return empty_plan()
    74→
    75→    return data  # type: ignore[return-value]
    76→
    77→
    78→def save_plan(plan: PlanModel | dict, path: Path | None = None) -> None:
    79→    """Validate and save plan to disk atomically."""
    80→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    81→    plan["updated"] = utc_now()
    82→    validate_plan(plan)
    83→
    84→    plan_path = path or PLAN_FILE
    85→    plan_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    86→
    87→    content = json.dumps(plan, indent=2, default=json_default) + "\n"
    88→
    89→    if plan_path.exists():
    90→        backup = plan_path.with_suffix(".json.bak")
    91→        try:
    92→            shutil.copy2(str(plan_path), str(backup))
    93→        except OSError as backup_ex:
    94→            logger.debug("Failed to create plan backup: %s", backup_ex)
    95→
    96→    try:
    97→        safe_write_text(plan_path, content)
    98→    except OSError as ex:
    99→        print(f"  Warning: Could not save plan: {ex}", file=sys.stderr)
   100→        raise
   101→
   102→
   103→def plan_path_for_state(state_path: Path) -> Path:
   104→    """Derive plan.json path from a state file path."""
   105→    return state_path.parent / "plan.json"
   106→
   107→
   108→def has_living_plan(path: Path | None = None) -> bool:
   109→    """Return True if a plan.json exists and has user intent."""
   110→    plan_path = path or PLAN_FILE
   111→    if not plan_path.exists():
   112→        return False
   113→    plan = load_plan(plan_path)
   114→    return bool(
   115→        plan.get("queue_order")
   116→        or plan.get("overrides")
   117→        or plan.get("clusters")
   118→    )
   119→
   120→
   121→__all__ = [
   122→    "PLAN_FILE",
   123→    "has_living_plan",
   124→    "load_plan",
   125→    "plan_path_for_state",
   126→    "save_plan",
   127→]
   128→

## Implementation Plan: Standardized Plan Staleness/Invalidation System

### 1. Problem Summary

The plan staleness detection works via the `synthesis::pending` + `review_finding_snapshot_hash` mechanism, but has three gaps:

- **Review import is plan-unaware**: `do_import()` saves state but never loads or reconciles the plan. After review import, `synthesis::pending` is NOT injected until the next scan runs `_reconcile_plan_post_scan()`.
- **`resolve` has no synthesis check**: Users can keep resolving items from a stale plan without any warning.
- **`status` and `show` don't display synthesis warnings**: Only `next` calls `print_synthesis_guardrail_banner()`.

### 2. Design Approach

The existing `synthesis::pending` + hash-comparison mechanism is solid. The design extends it with:

1. A **single detection function** (`is_synthesis_stale()`) that encapsulates the staleness check without side-effects.
2. A **single guardrail function** (`check_synthesis_guardrail()`) that replaces and subsumes `print_synthesis_guardrail_banner()` with configurable severity levels (info, warn, gate).
3. **Plan reconciliation after review import** by extracting the relevant sync logic from `_reconcile_plan_post_scan()` into a reusable helper.

### 3. Changes by File

#### 3A. Engine Layer: `desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py`

**Add** a pure detection function that checks staleness without mutating anything.

```python
def is_synthesis_stale(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> bool:
    """Return True when plan needs re-synthesis.

    Checks two conditions:
    1. synthesis::pending is already in the queue (explicitly flagged stale).
    2. The review finding snapshot hash has changed since last synthesis
       (stale but not yet flagged).
    """
    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    if SYNTHESIS_ID in order:
        return True

    meta = plan.get("epic_synthesis_meta", {})
    last_hash = meta.get("finding_snapshot_hash", "")
    if not last_hash:
        # No prior synthesis has been completed; not stale per se,
        # but sync_synthesis_needed will handle injection if findings exist.
        return False

    current_hash = review_finding_snapshot_hash(state)
    return bool(current_hash and current_hash != last_hash)
```

Add `"is_synthesis_stale"` to `__all__`.

#### 3B. Facade: `desloppify/engine/plan.py`

**Add re-export** of `is_synthesis_stale` from `stale_dimensions`.

```python
from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_dimensions import (
    ...
    is_synthesis_stale,
    ...
)
```

Add to `__all__`.

#### 3C. Guardrail Helpers: `desloppify/app/commands/helpers/guardrails.py`

**Expand** the module from a single print function to a two-level guardrail system.

Keep `print_synthesis_guardrail_banner()` for backward compatibility but have it delegate to the new function.

```python
"""Shared synthesis guardrail helpers for command entrypoints."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from typing import Literal

from desloppify.core.exception_sets import PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS
from desloppify.core.output_api import colorize
from desloppify.engine.plan import (
    has_living_plan,
    is_synthesis_stale,
    load_plan,
    synthesis_phase_banner,
    SYNTHESIS_ID,
)


def check_synthesis_guardrail(
    *,
    plan: dict | None = None,
    state: dict | None = None,
    severity: Literal["info", "warn", "gate"] = "info",
    command: str = "",
) -> bool:
    """Unified synthesis staleness guardrail.

    Severity levels:
      - "info": print yellow banner if stale (existing behavior). Returns True if stale.
      - "warn": print yellow banner with stronger wording. Returns True if stale.
      - "gate": print red error and sys.exit(1). Never returns True.

    Returns False when plan is not stale or no plan exists.
    """
    try:
        if not has_living_plan():
            return False
        resolved_plan = plan if isinstance(plan, dict) else load_plan()
        # Quick check: is synthesis::pending in queue?
        banner = synthesis_phase_banner(resolved_plan)
        if not banner:
            # Check hash-level staleness (catches the review-import gap)
            if state is not None and is_synthesis_stale(resolved_plan, state):
                banner = (
                    "Synthesis needed -- data has changed since last synthesis. "
                    "Run: desloppify plan synthesize"
                )
            else:
                return False
    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
        print(
            colorize(
                "  Warning: synthesis guardrail unavailable "
                f"({exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}).",
                "yellow",
            ),
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return False

    if severity == "gate":
        print(colorize(f"\n  {banner}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
        print(
            colorize(
                "  Re-synthesis is required before continuing to work the queue.",
                "red",
            ),
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        print(
            colorize(
                "  Run: desloppify plan synthesize",
                "dim",
            ),
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(1)

    color = "yellow"
    print(colorize(f"  {banner}", color))
    return True


def print_synthesis_guardrail_banner(*, plan: dict | None = None) -> None:
    """Print synthesis phase guardrail banner (backward-compatible wrapper)."""
    check_synthesis_guardrail(plan=plan, severity="info")


__all__ = [
    "check_synthesis_guardrail",
    "print_synthesis_guardrail_banner",
]
```

### 5. Tests

New test file: `desloppify/tests/plan/test_synthesis_staleness.py`

Tests for `is_synthesis_stale()`:
- Returns False when no plan or empty plan
- Returns True when `synthesis::pending` in queue
- Returns True when hash changed (review findings differ from stored hash)
- Returns False when hash matches
- Returns False when no prior synthesis (empty last_hash)

Tests for `check_synthesis_guardrail()`:
- Severity "info" prints banner, returns True when stale
- Severity "warn" prints banner, returns True when stale
- Severity "gate" calls sys.exit(1) when stale
- Returns False when plan is not stale
- Returns False when no living plan exists
- Handles PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS gracefully

Tests for review import plan sync:
- After `do_import()`, `synthesis::pending` is injected into plan queue when review findings change
- After `do_import()`, plan is not modified when findings haven't changed
- Plan sync failure doesn't block the import

### 6. Design Tradeoffs

**Why "warn" not "gate" for resolve?** A gate would be safer but more disruptive. The queue-order guard already provides structural protection. Starting with warn lets us observe if users actually ignore the warning before escalating to a gate.

**Why not add a scan-findings hash?** The current system only tracks review-finding hashes because scan results are directly reconciled by `reconcile_plan_after_scan()` (which runs inline during scan). The gap is specifically about review imports, which bypass the reconciliation path. Adding a scan-findings hash would be over-engineering.

**Why function-level imports in cmd files?** This follows the existing pattern (see `_reconcile_plan_post_scan` in scan_workflow.py) and avoids import cycles in the command layer.

**Why not a new module for the reconciliation helper?** The sync logic is only 15 lines. Extracting it to a shared module would be premature abstraction. If future commands also need post-mutation plan sync, it would be time to extract a `reconcile_plan_after_mutation(state)` helper.

   287→def _validate_run_dir(run_dir: Path) -> tuple[dict, Path, str]:
   288→    """Validate run directory, load summary, and return (summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path).
   289→
   290→    Exits with error message on any validation failure.
   291→    """
   292→    if not run_dir.is_dir():
   293→        print(colorize(f"  Error: run directory not found: {run_dir}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   294→        sys.exit(1)
   295→
   296→    summary_path = run_dir / "run_summary.json"
   297→    if not summary_path.exists():
   298→        print(colorize(f"  Error: no run_summary.json in {run_dir}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   299→        sys.exit(1)
   300→    try:
   301→        summary = json.loads(summary_path.read_text())
   302→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   303→        print(colorize(f"  Error reading run summary: {exc}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   304→        sys.exit(1)
   305→
   306→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   307→    blind_packet_path = Path(str(summary.get("blind_packet", "")))
   308→    immutable_packet_path = str(summary.get("immutable_packet", ""))
   309→
   310→    if not successful:
   311→        print(colorize("  Error: no successful batches in run summary.", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   312→        sys.exit(1)
   313→    if not blind_packet_path.exists():
   314→        print(colorize(f"  Error: blind packet not found: {blind_packet_path}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   315→        sys.exit(1)
   316→
   317→    try:
   318→        packet = json.loads(Path(immutable_packet_path).read_text())
   319→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   320→        print(colorize(f"  Error reading immutable packet: {exc}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   321→        sys.exit(1)
   322→
   323→    summary["_packet"] = packet
   324→    return summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path

   327→def do_import_run(
   328→    run_dir_path: str,
   329→    state: dict,
   330→    lang,
   331→    state_file: str,
   332→    *,
   333→    config: dict | None = None,
   334→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   335→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   336→    scan_path: str = ".",
   337→) -> None:
   338→    """Re-import results from a completed run directory.
   339→
   340→    Replays the merge+provenance+import step that normally runs at the end of
   341→    ``--run-batches``.  Useful when the original pipeline was interrupted (e.g.
   342→    broken pipe from background execution) but all batch results completed.
   343→    """
   344→    run_dir = Path(run_dir_path)
   345→    summary, blind_packet_path, _immutable_path = _validate_run_dir(run_dir)
   346→
   347→    runner = str(summary.get("runner", "codex"))
   348→    stamp = str(summary.get("run_stamp", ""))
   349→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   350→    packet = summary.pop("_packet", {})
   351→    allowed_dims = {str(d) for d in packet.get("dimensions", []) if isinstance(d, str)}
   352→
   353→    # -- locate and parse raw batch results --
   354→    results_dir = run_dir / "results"
   355→    selected_indexes = [idx - 1 for idx in successful]  # convert 1-based to 0-based
   356→    output_files = {
   357→        idx: results_dir / f"batch-{idx + 1}.raw.txt"
   358→        for idx in selected_indexes
   359→    }
   360→
   361→    missing = [idx + 1 for idx in selected_indexes if not output_files[idx].exists()]
   362→    if missing:
   363→        print(colorize(f"  Error: missing result files for batches: {missing}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   364→        sys.exit(1)
   365→
   366→    batch_results, failures = runner_helpers_mod.collect_batch_results(
   367→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   368→        failures=[],
   369→        output_files=output_files,
   370→        allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
   371→        extract_payload_fn=lambda raw: batch_core_mod.extract_json_payload(raw, log_fn=log),
   372→        normalize_result_fn=lambda payload, dims: batch_core_mod.normalize_batch_result(
   373→            payload,
   374→            dims,
   375→            max_batch_findings=max_batch_findings_for_dimension_count(len(dims)),
   376→            abstraction_sub_axes=ABSTRACTION_SUB_AXES,
   377→        ),
   378→    )
   379→
   380→    if not batch_results:
   381→        print(colorize("  Error: no valid batch results could be parsed.", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   382→        sys.exit(1)
   383→
   384→    print(colorize(f"  Parsed {len(batch_results)} batch results from {run_dir}", "bold"))
   385→    if failures:
   386→        print(colorize(f"  Warning: {len(failures)} batches failed to parse: {[f + 1 for f in failures]}", "yellow"))
   387→
   388→    # -- merge --
   389→    merged = _merge_batch_results(batch_results)
   390→
   391→    # -- build provenance --
   392→    successful_indexes = [idx for idx in selected_indexes if idx not in set(failures)]
   393→    merged["provenance"] = runner_helpers_mod.build_batch_import_provenance(
   394→        runner=runner,
   395→        blind_packet_path=blind_packet_path,
   396→        run_stamp=stamp,
   397→        batch_indexes=successful_indexes,
   398→    )
   399→
   400→    # -- write merged output --
   401→    merged_path = run_dir / "holistic_findings_merged.json"
   402→    safe_write_text(merged_path, json.dumps(merged, indent=2) + "\n")
   403→    print(colorize(f"  Merged output: {merged_path}", "bold"))
   404→
   405→    # -- import with trusted source --
   406→    _do_import(
   407→        str(merged_path),
   408→        state,
   409→        lang,
   410→        state_file,
   411→        config=config,
   412→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   413→        trusted_assessment_source=True,
   414→        trusted_assessment_label=f"trusted import-run replay from {run_dir.name}",
   415→    )
   416→
   417→    # -- optional follow-up scan --
   418→    if scan_after_import:
   419→        lang_name = getattr(lang, "name", None) or str(getattr(lang, "lang", ""))
   420→        if lang_name:
   421→            runner_helpers_mod.run_followup_scan(
   422→                lang_name=lang_name,
   423→                scan_path=scan_path,
   424→                deps=runner_helpers_mod.FollowupScanDeps(
   425→                    project_root=_runtime_project_root(),
   426→                    timeout_seconds=FOLLOWUP_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   427→                    python_executable=sys.executable,

    21→    """Best-effort: force line-buffered review output for non-TTY runners."""
    22→    for stream_name in ("stdout", "stderr"):
    23→        stream = getattr(sys, stream_name, None)
    24→        reconfigure = getattr(stream, "reconfigure", None)
    25→        if not callable(reconfigure):

    28→            reconfigure(line_buffering=True, write_through=True)

   184→        return
   185→    review_rerun_preflight(state, args, state_file=state_file)
   186→    do_prepare(args, state, lang, state_file, config=runtime.config)

   188→
   189→def cmd_review(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   190→    """Prepare or import subjective code review findings."""
   191→    _enable_live_review_output()
   192→    runtime = command_runtime(args)

   204→    _run_review_mode(

    35→def parse_holistic_import_payload(
    36→    data: ReviewImportPayload | dict[str, Any],
    37→) -> tuple[list[ReviewFindingPayload], dict[str, Any] | None, list[str]]:
    38→    """Parse strict holistic import payload object."""

    43→def update_reviewed_file_cache(
    44→    state: dict[str, Any],
    45→    reviewed_files: list[str],
    46→    *,
    47→    project_root: Path | str | None = None,
    48→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
    49→) -> None:

    56→        hash_file_fn=hash_file,
    57→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
    58→    )
    59→
    60→
    61→_POSITIVE_PREFIXES = (
    62→    "good ",
    63→    "well ",
    64→    "strong ",
    65→    "clean ",
    66→    "excellent ",
    67→    "nice ",
    68→    "solid ",

    72→def _validate_and_build_findings(
    73→    findings_list: list[ReviewFindingPayload],
    74→    holistic_prompts: dict[str, Any],
    75→    lang_name: str,
    76→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    77→    """Validate raw holistic findings and build state-ready finding dicts.
    78→
    79→    Returns (review_findings, skipped, dismissed_concerns).
    80→    """
    81→    review_findings: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    82→    skipped: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    83→    dismissed_concerns: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    84→    allowed_dimensions = {
    85→        dim for dim in holistic_prompts if isinstance(dim, str) and dim.strip()
    86→    }
    87→
    88→    for idx, raw_finding in enumerate(findings_list):
    89→        finding, finding_errors = validate_review_finding_payload(
    90→            raw_finding,
    91→            label=f"findings[{idx}]",
    92→            allowed_dimensions=allowed_dimensions,
    93→            allow_dismissed=True,
    94→        )
    95→        if finding_errors:
    96→            skipped.append(
    97→                {
    98→                    "index": idx,
    99→                    "missing": finding_errors,
   100→                    "identifier": (
   101→                        raw_finding.get("identifier", "<none>")
   102→                        if isinstance(raw_finding, dict)
   103→                        else "<none>"
   104→                    ),
   105→                }
   106→            )
   107→            continue
   108→        assert finding is not None
   109→
   110→        # Handle dismissed concern verdicts (no dimension/summary required).
   111→        if finding.get("concern_verdict") == "dismissed":
   112→            fp = finding.get("concern_fingerprint", "")
   113→            if fp:
   114→                dismissed_concerns.append(
   115→                    {
   116→                        "fingerprint": fp,
   117→                        "concern_type": finding.get("concern_type", ""),
   118→                        "concern_file": finding.get("concern_file", ""),
   119→                        "reasoning": finding.get("reasoning", ""),
   120→                    }
   121→                )
   122→            continue
   123→
   124→        # Safety net: skip positive observations that slipped past the prompt.
   125→        summary_text = str(finding.get("summary", ""))
   126→        if summary_text.lower().startswith(_POSITIVE_PREFIXES):
   127→            skipped.append(
   128→                {
   129→                    "index": idx,
   130→                    "missing": ["positive observation (not a defect)"],
   131→                    "identifier": finding.get("identifier", "<none>"),
   132→                }
   133→            )
   134→            continue
   135→
   136→        dimension = finding["dimension"]
   137→
   138→        # Confirmed concern verdicts become "concerns" detector findings.
   139→        is_confirmed_concern = finding.get("concern_verdict") == "confirmed"
   140→        detector = "concerns" if is_confirmed_concern else "review"
   141→
   142→        content_hash = hashlib.sha256(summary_text.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
   143→        detail: dict[str, Any] = {
   144→            "holistic": True,
   145→            "dimension": dimension,
   146→            "related_files": finding["related_files"],
   147→            "evidence": finding["evidence"],
   148→            "suggestion": finding.get("suggestion", ""),
   149→            "reasoning": finding.get("reasoning", ""),
   150→        }
   151→        if is_confirmed_concern:
   152→            detail["concern_type"] = finding.get("concern_type", "")
   153→            detail["concern_verdict"] = "confirmed"
   154→
   155→        prefix = "concern" if is_confirmed_concern else "holistic"
   156→        file = finding.get("concern_file", "") if is_confirmed_concern else ""
   157→        confidence = normalize_review_confidence(finding.get("confidence", "low"))
   158→        imported = make_finding(
   159→            detector=detector,
   160→            file=file,
   161→            name=f"{prefix}::{dimension}::{finding['identifier']}::{content_hash}",
   162→            tier=review_tier(confidence, holistic=True),
   163→            confidence=confidence,
   164→            summary=summary_text,
   165→            detail=detail,
   166→        )
   167→        imported["lang"] = lang_name
   168→        review_findings.append(imported)
   169→
   170→    return review_findings, skipped, dismissed_concerns
   171→
   172→
   173→def _collect_imported_dimensions(
   174→    *,
   175→    findings_list: list[ReviewFindingPayload],
   176→    review_findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   177→    assessments: dict[str, Any] | None,
   178→    review_scope: ReviewScopePayload | dict[str, Any] | None,
   179→    valid_dimensions: set[str],
   180→) -> set[str]:
   181→    """Return normalized dimensions this import explicitly covered."""
   182→    imported_dimensions: set[str] = set()
   183→
   184→    if isinstance(review_scope, dict):
   185→        scope_dims = review_scope.get("imported_dimensions")
   186→        if isinstance(scope_dims, list):
   187→            for raw_dim in scope_dims:
   188→                normalized = normalize_dimension_name(str(raw_dim))
   189→                if normalized in valid_dimensions:
   190→                    imported_dimensions.add(normalized)
   191→
   192→    for finding in findings_list:
   193→        if not isinstance(finding, dict):
   194→            continue
   195→        normalized = normalize_dimension_name(str(finding.get("dimension", "")))
   196→        if normalized in valid_dimensions:
   197→            imported_dimensions.add(normalized)
   198→
   199→    for finding in review_findings:
   200→        detail = finding.get("detail")
   201→        if not isinstance(detail, dict):
   202→            continue
   203→        normalized = normalize_dimension_name(str(detail.get("dimension", "")))
   204→        if normalized in valid_dimensions:
   205→            imported_dimensions.add(normalized)
   206→
   207→    for raw_dim in (assessments or {}):
   208→        normalized = normalize_dimension_name(str(raw_dim))
   209→        if normalized in valid_dimensions:
   210→            imported_dimensions.add(normalized)
   211→
   212→    return imported_dimensions
   213→
   214→
   215→def _auto_resolve_stale_holistic(
   216→    state: dict[str, Any],
   217→    new_ids: set[str],
   218→    diff: dict[str, Any],
   219→    utc_now_fn,
   220→    *,
   221→    imported_dimensions: set[str] | None = None,
   222→    full_sweep_included: bool | None = None,
   223→) -> None:
   224→    """Auto-resolve open holistic findings not present in the latest import."""
   225→    scope_dimensions = {
   226→        normalize_dimension_name(dim)
   227→        for dim in (imported_dimensions or set())
   228→        if isinstance(dim, str) and dim.strip()
   229→    }
   230→    scoped_reimport = full_sweep_included is False
   231→    # Partial re-import with unknown dimension scope: do not auto-resolve.
   232→    if scoped_reimport and not scope_dimensions:
   233→        return
   234→
   235→    def _should_resolve(finding: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
   236→        if finding.get("detector") not in ("review", "concerns"):
   237→            return False
   238→        detail = finding.get("detail")
   239→        if not isinstance(detail, dict) or not detail.get("holistic"):
   240→            return False
   241→        if not scoped_reimport:
   242→            return True
   243→        dimension = normalize_dimension_name(str(detail.get("dimension", "")))
   244→        return dimension in scope_dimensions
   245→
   246→    auto_resolve_review_findings(
   247→        state,
   248→        new_ids=new_ids,
   249→        diff=diff,
   250→        note="not reported in latest holistic re-import",
   251→        should_resolve=_should_resolve,
   252→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   253→    )
   254→
   255→
   256→def import_holistic_findings(
   257→    findings_data: ReviewImportPayload,
   258→    state: dict[str, Any],
   259→    lang_name: str,
   260→    *,
   261→    project_root: Path | str | None = None,
   262→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   263→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   264→    """Import holistic (codebase-wide) findings into state."""
   265→    payload: ReviewImportEnvelope = parse_review_import_payload(
   266→        findings_data,
   267→        mode_name="Holistic",
   268→    )
   269→    findings_list = payload.findings
   270→    assessments = payload.assessments
   271→    reviewed_files = payload.reviewed_files
   272→    review_scope = findings_data.get("review_scope", {})
   273→    if not isinstance(review_scope, dict):
   274→        review_scope = {}
   275→    scope_full_sweep = review_scope.get("full_sweep_included")
   276→    if not isinstance(scope_full_sweep, bool):
   277→        scope_full_sweep = None
   278→    if assessments:
   279→        store_assessments(
   280→            state,
   281→            assessments,
   282→            source="holistic",
   283→            utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   284→        )
   285→
   286→    _, holistic_prompts, _ = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name)
   287→    valid_dimensions = {
   288→        normalize_dimension_name(dim)
   289→        for dim in holistic_prompts
   290→        if isinstance(dim, str)
   291→    }
   292→    review_findings, skipped, dismissed_concerns = _validate_and_build_findings(
   293→        findings_list, holistic_prompts, lang_name
   294→    )
   295→    imported_dimensions = _collect_imported_dimensions(
   296→        findings_list=findings_list,
   297→        review_findings=review_findings,
   298→        assessments=assessments if isinstance(assessments, dict) else None,
   299→        review_scope=review_scope,
   300→        valid_dimensions=valid_dimensions,
   301→    )
   302→
   303→    # Store dismissed concern verdicts for suppression in future concern generation.
   304→    if dismissed_concerns:
   305→        from desloppify.engine.concerns import generate_concerns
   306→
   307→        store = state.setdefault("concern_dismissals", {})
   308→        now = utc_now_fn()
   309→        # Compute current concerns to get source_finding_ids for each fingerprint.
   310→        current_concerns = generate_concerns(state, lang_name=lang_name)
   311→        concern_sources = {
   312→            c.fingerprint: list(c.source_findings) for c in current_concerns
   313→        }
   314→        for dc in dismissed_concerns:
   315→            fp = dc["fingerprint"]
   316→            store[fp] = {
   317→                "dismissed_at": now,
   318→                "reasoning": dc.get("reasoning", ""),
   319→                "concern_type": dc.get("concern_type", ""),
   320→                "concern_file": dc.get("concern_file", ""),
   321→                "source_finding_ids": concern_sources.get(fp, []),
   322→            }
   323→
   324→    potentials = _lang_potentials(state, lang_name)
   325→    existing_review = potentials.get("review", 0)
   326→    potentials["review"] = max(existing_review, HOLISTIC_POTENTIAL)
   327→
   328→    concern_count = sum(1 for f in review_findings if f.get("detector") == "concerns")
   329→    if concern_count:
   330→        potentials["concerns"] = max(potentials.get("concerns", 0), concern_count)
   331→
   332→    merge_potentials_dict: dict[str, int] = {"review": potentials.get("review", 0)}
   333→    if potentials.get("concerns", 0) > 0:
   334→        merge_potentials_dict["concerns"] = potentials["concerns"]
   335→
   336→    diff = merge_scan(
   337→        state,
   338→        review_findings,
   339→        options=MergeScanOptions(
   340→            lang=lang_name,
   341→            potentials=merge_potentials_dict,
   342→            merge_potentials=True,
   343→        ),
   344→    )
   345→
   346→    new_ids = {finding["id"] for finding in review_findings}
   347→    _auto_resolve_stale_holistic(
   348→        state,
   349→        new_ids,
   350→        diff,
   351→        utc_now_fn,
   352→        imported_dimensions=imported_dimensions,
   353→        full_sweep_included=scope_full_sweep,
   354→    )
   355→
   356→    if skipped:
   357→        diff["skipped"] = len(skipped)
   358→        diff["skipped_details"] = skipped
   359→
   360→    update_reviewed_file_cache(
   361→        state,
   362→        reviewed_files,
   363→        project_root=project_root,
   364→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   365→    )
   366→    resolve_reviewed_file_coverage_findings(
   367→        state,
   368→        diff,
   369→        reviewed_files,
   370→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   371→    )
   372→    update_holistic_review_cache(
   373→        state,
   374→        findings_list,
   375→        lang_name=lang_name,
   376→        review_scope=review_scope,
   377→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   378→    )
   379→    resolve_holistic_coverage_findings(state, diff, utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn)
   380→
   381→    # Clean up dismissals whose source findings were all resolved — runs after
   382→    # all finding mutations (merge_scan, auto_resolve, coverage resolve) so it
   383→    # sees the final state.
   384→    from desloppify.engine.concerns import cleanup_stale_dismissals
   385→
   386→    cleanup_stale_dismissals(state)
   387→
   388→    return diff
   389→
   390→
   391→def _resolve_total_files(state: dict[str, Any], lang_name: str | None) -> int:
   392→    """Best-effort total file count from codebase_metrics or review cache."""
   393→    review_cache = state.get("review_cache", {})
   394→    fallback = len(review_cache.get("files", {}))
   395→
   396→    codebase_metrics = state.get("codebase_metrics", {})
   397→    if not isinstance(codebase_metrics, dict):
   398→        return fallback
   399→
   400→    # Try language-specific metrics first, then global.
   401→    sources = []
   402→    if lang_name:
   403→        lang_metrics = codebase_metrics.get(lang_name)
   404→        if isinstance(lang_metrics, dict):
   405→            sources.append(lang_metrics)
   406→    sources.append(codebase_metrics)
   407→
   408→    for source in sources:
   409→        metric_total = source.get("total_files")
   410→        if isinstance(metric_total, int) and metric_total > 0:
   411→            return metric_total
   412→
   413→    return fallback
   414→
   415→
   416→def update_holistic_review_cache(
   417→    state: dict[str, Any],
   418→    findings_data: list[dict],
   419→    *,
   420→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   421→    review_scope: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   422→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   423→) -> None:
   424→    """Store holistic review metadata in review_cache."""
   425→    review_cache = state.setdefault("review_cache", {})
   426→    now = utc_now_fn()
   427→    _, holistic_prompts, _ = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name or "")
   428→
   429→    valid = [
   430→        finding
   431→        for finding in findings_data
   432→        if all(
   433→            key in finding
   434→            for key in ("dimension", "identifier", "summary", "confidence")
   435→        )
   436→        and finding["dimension"] in holistic_prompts
   437→    ]
   438→
   439→    resolved_total_files: int
   440→    total_override = (
   441→        review_scope.get("total_files")
   442→        if isinstance(review_scope, dict)
   443→        else None
   444→    )
   445→    if (
   446→        isinstance(total_override, int)
   447→        and not isinstance(total_override, bool)
   448→        and total_override > 0
   449→    ):
   450→        resolved_total_files = total_override
   451→    else:
   452→        resolved_total_files = _resolve_total_files(state, lang_name)
   453→
   454→    holistic_entry: dict[str, Any] = {
   455→        "reviewed_at": now,
   456→        "file_count_at_review": resolved_total_files,
   457→        "finding_count": len(valid),
   458→    }
   459→    if isinstance(review_scope, dict):
   460→        reviewed_files_count = review_scope.get("reviewed_files_count")
   461→        if (
   462→            isinstance(reviewed_files_count, int)
   463→            and not isinstance(reviewed_files_count, bool)
   464→            and reviewed_files_count >= 0
   465→        ):
   466→            holistic_entry["reviewed_files_count"] = reviewed_files_count
   467→        full_sweep_included = review_scope.get("full_sweep_included")
   468→        if isinstance(full_sweep_included, bool):
   469→            holistic_entry["full_sweep_included"] = full_sweep_included
   470→
   471→    review_cache["holistic"] = holistic_entry
   472→
   473→
   474→def resolve_holistic_coverage_findings(
   475→    state: dict[str, Any],
   476→    diff: dict[str, Any],
   477→    *,
   478→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   479→) -> None:
   480→    """Resolve stale holistic coverage entries after successful holistic import."""
   481→    now = utc_now_fn()
   482→    for finding in state.get("findings", {}).values():
   483→        if finding.get("status") != "open":
   484→            continue
   485→        if finding.get("detector") != "subjective_review":
   486→            continue
   487→
   488→        finding_id = finding.get("id", "")
   489→        if (
   490→            "::holistic_unreviewed" not in finding_id
   491→            and "::holistic_stale" not in finding_id
   492→        ):
   493→            continue
   494→
   495→        finding["status"] = "auto_resolved"
   496→        finding["resolved_at"] = now
   497→        finding["note"] = "resolved by holistic review import"
   498→        finding["resolution_attestation"] = {
   499→            "kind": "agent_import",
   500→            "text": "Holistic review refreshed; coverage marker superseded",
   501→            "attested_at": now,
   502→            "scan_verified": False,
   503→        }
   504→        diff["auto_resolved"] += 1
   505→
   506→
   507→def resolve_reviewed_file_coverage_findings(
   508→    state: dict[str, Any],
   509→    diff: dict[str, Any],
   510→    reviewed_files: list[str],
   511→    *,
   512→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   513→) -> None:
   514→    """Resolve per-file subjective coverage markers for freshly reviewed files."""
   515→    if not reviewed_files:
   516→        return
   517→
   518→    reviewed_set = {path for path in reviewed_files if isinstance(path, str) and path}
   519→    if not reviewed_set:
   520→        return
   521→
   522→    now = utc_now_fn()
   523→    for finding in state.get("findings", {}).values():
   524→        if finding.get("status") != "open":
   525→            continue
   526→        if finding.get("detector") != "subjective_review":
   527→            continue
   528→
   529→        finding_id = finding.get("id", "")
   530→        if "::holistic_unreviewed" in finding_id or "::holistic_stale" in finding_id:
   531→            continue
   532→
   533→        finding_file = finding.get("file", "")
   534→        if finding_file not in reviewed_set:
   535→            continue
   536→
   537→        finding["status"] = "auto_resolved"
   538→        finding["resolved_at"] = now
   539→        finding["note"] = "resolved by reviewed_files cache refresh"
   540→        finding["resolution_attestation"] = {
   541→            "kind": "agent_import",
   542→            "text": "Per-file review cache refreshed for this file",
   543→            "attested_at": now,
   544→            "scan_verified": False,
   545→        }
   546→        diff["auto_resolved"] += 1
   547→

1→"""Post-scan plan reconciliation — handle finding churn."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     6→from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
     7→
     8→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import EPIC_PREFIX, PlanModel, SupersededEntry, ensure_plan_defaults
     9→from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_dimensions import SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX, SYNTHESIS_ID
    10→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel, utc_now
    11→
    12→
    13→SUPERSEDED_TTL_DAYS = 90
    14→
    15→
    16→@dataclass
    17→class ReconcileResult:
    18→    """Summary of changes made during reconciliation."""
    19→
    20→    superseded: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    21→    pruned: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    22→    resurfaced: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    23→    changes: int = 0
    24→
    25→
    26→def _find_candidates(
    27→    state: StateModel, detector: str, file: str
    28→) -> list[str]:
    29→    """Find open findings that could be remaps for a disappeared finding."""
    30→    candidates: list[str] = []
    31→    for fid, finding in state.get("findings", {}).items():
    32→        if finding.get("status") != "open":
    33→            continue
    34→        if finding.get("detector") == detector and finding.get("file") == file:
    35→            candidates.append(fid)
    36→    return candidates
    37→
    38→
    39→def _is_finding_alive(state: StateModel, finding_id: str) -> bool:
    40→    """Return True if the finding exists and is open."""
    41→    finding = state.get("findings", {}).get(finding_id)
    42→    if finding is None:
    43→        return False
    44→    return finding.get("status") == "open"
    45→
    46→
    47→def _supersede_id(
    48→    plan: PlanModel,
    49→    state: StateModel,
    50→    finding_id: str,
    51→    now: str,
    52→) -> bool:
    53→    """Move a disappeared finding to superseded. Returns True if changed."""
    54→    finding = state.get("findings", {}).get(finding_id)
    55→    detector = ""
    56→    file = ""
    57→    summary = ""
    58→    if finding:
    59→        detector = finding.get("detector", "")
    60→        file = finding.get("file", "")
    61→        summary = finding.get("summary", "")
    62→
    63→    candidates = _find_candidates(state, detector, file) if detector else []
    64→    # Don't include the original in candidates
    65→    candidates = [c for c in candidates if c != finding_id]
    66→
    67→    entry: SupersededEntry = {
    68→        "original_id": finding_id,
    69→        "original_detector": detector,
    70→        "original_file": file,
    71→        "original_summary": summary,
    72→        "status": "superseded",
    73→        "superseded_at": now,
    74→        "remapped_to": None,
    75→        "candidates": candidates[:5],
    76→    }
    77→
    78→    # Preserve any existing override note
    79→    override = plan.get("overrides", {}).get(finding_id)
    80→    if override and override.get("note"):
    81→        entry["note"] = override["note"]
    82→
    83→    plan["superseded"][finding_id] = entry
    84→
    85→    # Remove from queue_order, skipped, cluster finding_ids
    86→    order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    87→    skipped: dict = plan.get("skipped", {})
    88→    if finding_id in order:
    89→        order.remove(finding_id)
    90→    skipped.pop(finding_id, None)
    91→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    92→        ids = cluster.get("finding_ids", [])
    93→        if finding_id in ids:
    94→            ids.remove(finding_id)
    95→
    96→    # Clear stale cluster reference from override
    97→    override = plan.get("overrides", {}).get(finding_id)
    98→    if override and override.get("cluster"):
    99→        override["cluster"] = None
   100→        override["updated_at"] = now
   101→
   102→    return True
   103→
   104→
   105→def _prune_old_superseded(plan: PlanModel, now_dt: datetime) -> list[str]:
   106→    """Remove superseded entries older than TTL. Returns pruned IDs."""
   107→    superseded = plan.get("superseded", {})
   108→    cutoff = now_dt - timedelta(days=SUPERSEDED_TTL_DAYS)
   109→    to_prune: list[str] = []
   110→
   111→    for fid, entry in superseded.items():
   112→        ts = entry.get("superseded_at", "")
   113→        try:
   114→            entry_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(ts)
   115→            if entry_dt.tzinfo is None:
   116→                entry_dt = entry_dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
   117→            if entry_dt < cutoff:
   118→                to_prune.append(fid)
   119→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   120→            to_prune.append(fid)
   121→
   122→    for fid in to_prune:
   123→        superseded.pop(fid, None)
   124→        # Also clean up stale overrides
   125→        plan.get("overrides", {}).pop(fid, None)
   126→
   127→    return to_prune
   128→
   129→
   130→def reconcile_plan_after_scan(
   131→    plan: PlanModel,
   132→    state: StateModel,
   133→) -> ReconcileResult:
   134→    """Reconcile plan against current state after a scan.
   135→
   136→    Finds IDs referenced in the plan that no longer exist or are no longer
   137→    open, moves them to superseded, and prunes old superseded entries.
   138→    """
   139→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   140→    result = ReconcileResult()
   141→    now = utc_now()
   142→    now_dt = datetime.now(UTC)
   143→
   144→    # Collect all finding IDs referenced by the plan
   145→    referenced_ids: set[str] = set()
   146→    referenced_ids.update(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   147→    referenced_ids.update(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   148→    for override_id in plan.get("overrides", {}):
   149→        referenced_ids.add(override_id)
   150→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   151→        referenced_ids.update(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   152→
   153→    # Exclude already-superseded IDs and synthetic IDs (managed by stale_dimensions)
   154→    already_superseded = set(plan.get("superseded", {}).keys())
   155→    referenced_ids -= already_superseded
   156→    referenced_ids = {
   157→        fid for fid in referenced_ids
   158→        if not fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   159→        and fid != SYNTHESIS_ID
   160→    }
   161→
   162→    # Check each referenced ID
   163→    for fid in sorted(referenced_ids):
   164→        if not _is_finding_alive(state, fid):
   165→            if _supersede_id(plan, state, fid, now):
   166→                result.superseded.append(fid)
   167→                result.changes += 1
   168→
   169→    # Reconcile epic clusters: remove dead findings, delete empty epics
   170→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   171→    epic_names_to_delete: list[str] = []
   172→    for name, cluster in list(clusters.items()):
   173→        if not name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX):
   174→            continue
   175→        finding_ids = cluster.get("finding_ids", [])
   176→        alive_ids = [fid for fid in finding_ids if _is_finding_alive(state, fid)]
   177→        if alive_ids != finding_ids:
   178→            cluster["finding_ids"] = alive_ids
   179→            result.changes += 1
   180→        if not alive_ids:
   181→            epic_names_to_delete.append(name)
   182→    for name in epic_names_to_delete:
   183→        clusters.pop(name, None)
   184→        result.changes += 1
   185→
   186→    # Resurface stale temporary skips
   187→    scan_count = state.get("scan_count", 0)
   188→    from desloppify.engine._plan.operations import resurface_stale_skips
   189→
   190→    resurfaced = resurface_stale_skips(plan, scan_count)
   191→    if resurfaced:
   192→        result.resurfaced = resurfaced
   193→        result.changes += len(resurfaced)
   194→
   195→    # Prune old superseded entries
   196→    pruned = _prune_old_superseded(plan, now_dt)
   197→    result.pruned = pruned
   198→    result.changes += len(pruned)
   199→
   200→    # Log reconciliation if any changes were made
   201→    if result.changes > 0:
   202→        from desloppify.engine._plan.operations import append_log_entry
   203→
   204→        append_log_entry(
   205→            plan,
   206→            "reconcile",
   207→            finding_ids=result.superseded,
   208→            actor="system",
   209→            detail={
   210→                "superseded_count": len(result.superseded),
   211→                "pruned_count": len(result.pruned),
   212→                "resurfaced_count": len(result.resurfaced),
   213→            },
   214→        )
   215→
   216→    return result
   217→
   218→
   219→__all__ = [
   220→    "ReconcileResult",
   221→    "reconcile_plan_after_scan",
   222→]
   223→

   165→
   166→def _migrate_epics_to_clusters(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   167→    """Migrate v3 top-level ``epics`` dict into ``clusters`` (v4 unification)."""
   168→    epics = plan.pop("epics", None)
   169→    if not isinstance(epics, dict) or not epics:
   170→        return
   171→    clusters = plan["clusters"]
   172→    now = utc_now()
   173→    for name, epic in epics.items():
   174→        if not isinstance(epic, dict):
   175→            continue
   176→        if name in clusters:
   177→            continue  # don't overwrite existing cluster
   178→        clusters[name] = {
   179→            "name": name,
   180→            "description": epic.get("thesis", ""),
   181→            "finding_ids": epic.get("finding_ids", []),
   182→            "auto": True,
   183→            "cluster_key": f"epic::{name}",
   184→            "action": f"desloppify plan focus {name}",
   185→            "user_modified": False,
   186→            "created_at": epic.get("created_at", now),
   187→            "updated_at": epic.get("updated_at", now),
   188→            # Epic-specific fields
   189→            "thesis": epic.get("thesis", ""),
   190→            "direction": epic.get("direction", "simplify"),
   191→            "root_cause": epic.get("root_cause", ""),
   192→            "supersedes": epic.get("supersedes", []),
   193→            "dismissed": epic.get("dismissed", []),
   194→            "agent_safe": epic.get("agent_safe", False),
   195→            "dependency_order": epic.get("dependency_order", 999),
   196→            "action_steps": epic.get("action_steps", []),
   197→            "source_clusters": epic.get("source_clusters", []),
   198→            "status": epic.get("status", "pending"),
   199→            "synthesis_version": epic.get("synthesis_version", 0),
   200→        }
   201→
   202→
   203→def ensure_plan_defaults(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   204→    """Normalize a loaded plan to ensure all keys exist.
   205→
   206→    Handles migration from v1 (deferred list) to v2 (skipped dict),
   207→    and v3 (top-level epics) to v4 (epics unified into clusters).
   208→    """
   209→    defaults = empty_plan()
   210→    for key, value in defaults.items():
   211→        plan.setdefault(key, value)
   212→
   213→    _ensure_container_types(plan)
   214→    _migrate_deferred_to_skipped(plan)
   215→    _migrate_epics_to_clusters(plan)
   216→    _normalize_cluster_defaults(plan)
   217→
   218→
   219→def synthesis_clusters(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Cluster]:
   220→    """Return clusters whose name starts with ``EPIC_PREFIX``."""
   221→    return {
   222→        name: cluster
   223→        for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items()
   224→        if name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX)
   225→    }
   226→
   227→
   228→def validate_plan(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   229→    """Raise ValueError when plan invariants are violated."""
   230→    if not isinstance(plan.get("version"), int):
   231→        raise ValueError("plan.version must be an int")
   232→    if not isinstance(plan.get("queue_order"), list):
   233→        raise ValueError("plan.queue_order must be a list")
   234→
   235→    # No ID should appear in both queue_order and skipped
   236→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   237→    overlap = set(plan["queue_order"]) & skipped_ids
   238→    if overlap:
   239→        raise ValueError(
   240→            f"IDs cannot appear in both queue_order and skipped: {sorted(overlap)}"
   241→        )
   242→
   243→    # Validate skip entry kinds
   244→    for fid, entry in plan.get("skipped", {}).items():
   245→        kind = entry.get("kind")
   246→        if kind not in VALID_SKIP_KINDS:
   247→            raise ValueError(
   248→                f"Invalid skip kind {kind!r} for {fid}; must be one of {sorted(VALID_SKIP_KINDS)}"
   249→            )
   250→
   251→
   252→__all__ = [
   253→    "EPIC_PREFIX",
   254→    "ExecutionLogEntry",
   255→    "PLAN_VERSION",
   256→    "Cluster",
   257→    "ItemOverride",
   258→    "PlanModel",
   259→    "SkipEntry",
   260→    "SupersededEntry",
   261→    "VALID_EPIC_DIRECTIONS",

   263→    "empty_plan",
   264→    "ensure_plan_defaults",
   265→    "synthesis_clusters",

   267→]

1→"""Post-scan plan reconciliation — handle finding churn."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     6→from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
     7→
     8→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import EPIC_PREFIX, PlanModel, SupersededEntry, ensure_plan_defaults
     9→from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_dimensions import SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX, SYNTHESIS_ID
    10→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel, utc_now
    11→
    12→
    13→SUPERSEDED_TTL_DAYS = 90
    14→
    15→
    16→@dataclass
    17→class ReconcileResult:
    18→    """Summary of changes made during reconciliation."""
    19→
    20→    superseded: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    21→    pruned: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    22→    resurfaced: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    23→    changes: int = 0
    24→
    25→
    26→def _find_candidates(
    27→    state: StateModel, detector: str, file: str
    28→) -> list[str]:
    29→    """Find open findings that could be remaps for a disappeared finding."""
    30→    candidates: list[str] = []
    31→    for fid, finding in state.get("findings", {}).items():
    32→        if finding.get("status") != "open":
    33→            continue
    34→        if finding.get("detector") == detector and finding.get("file") == file:
    35→            candidates.append(fid)
    36→    return candidates
    37→
    38→
    39→def _is_finding_alive(state: StateModel, finding_id: str) -> bool:
    40→    """Return True if the finding exists and is open."""
    41→    finding = state.get("findings", {}).get(finding_id)
    42→    if finding is None:
    43→        return False
    44→    return finding.get("status") == "open"
    45→
    46→
    47→def _supersede_id(
    48→    plan: PlanModel,
    49→    state: StateModel,
    50→    finding_id: str,
    51→    now: str,
    52→) -> bool:
    53→    """Move a disappeared finding to superseded. Returns True if changed."""
    54→    finding = state.get("findings", {}).get(finding_id)
    55→    detector = ""
    56→    file = ""
    57→    summary = ""
    58→    if finding:
    59→        detector = finding.get("detector", "")
    60→        file = finding.get("file", "")
    61→        summary = finding.get("summary", "")
    62→
    63→    candidates = _find_candidates(state, detector, file) if detector else []
    64→    # Don't include the original in candidates
    65→    candidates = [c for c in candidates if c != finding_id]
    66→
    67→    entry: SupersededEntry = {
    68→        "original_id": finding_id,
    69→        "original_detector": detector,
    70→        "original_file": file,
    71→        "original_summary": summary,
    72→        "status": "superseded",
    73→        "superseded_at": now,
    74→        "remapped_to": None,
    75→        "candidates": candidates[:5],
    76→    }
    77→
    78→    # Preserve any existing override note
    79→    override = plan.get("overrides", {}).get(finding_id)
    80→    if override and override.get("note"):
    81→        entry["note"] = override["note"]
    82→
    83→    plan["superseded"][finding_id] = entry
    84→
    85→    # Remove from queue_order, skipped, cluster finding_ids
    86→    order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    87→    skipped: dict = plan.get("skipped", {})
    88→    if finding_id in order:
    89→        order.remove(finding_id)
    90→    skipped.pop(finding_id, None)
    91→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    92→        ids = cluster.get("finding_ids", [])
    93→        if finding_id in ids:
    94→            ids.remove(finding_id)
    95→
    96→    # Clear stale cluster reference from override
    97→    override = plan.get("overrides", {}).get(finding_id)
    98→    if override and override.get("cluster"):
    99→        override["cluster"] = None
   100→        override["updated_at"] = now
   101→
   102→    return True
   103→
   104→
   105→def _prune_old_superseded(plan: PlanModel, now_dt: datetime) -> list[str]:
   106→    """Remove superseded entries older than TTL. Returns pruned IDs."""
   107→    superseded = plan.get("superseded", {})
   108→    cutoff = now_dt - timedelta(days=SUPERSEDED_TTL_DAYS)
   109→    to_prune: list[str] = []
   110→
   111→    for fid, entry in superseded.items():
   112→        ts = entry.get("superseded_at", "")
   113→        try:
   114→            entry_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(ts)
   115→            if entry_dt.tzinfo is None:
   116→                entry_dt = entry_dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
   117→            if entry_dt < cutoff:
   118→                to_prune.append(fid)
   119→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   120→            to_prune.append(fid)
   121→
   122→    for fid in to_prune:
   123→        superseded.pop(fid, None)
   124→        # Also clean up stale overrides
   125→        plan.get("overrides", {}).pop(fid, None)
   126→
   127→    return to_prune
   128→
   129→
   130→def reconcile_plan_after_scan(
   131→    plan: PlanModel,
   132→    state: StateModel,
   133→) -> ReconcileResult:
   134→    """Reconcile plan against current state after a scan.
   135→
   136→    Finds IDs referenced in the plan that no longer exist or are no longer
   137→    open, moves them to superseded, and prunes old superseded entries.
   138→    """
   139→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   140→    result = ReconcileResult()
   141→    now = utc_now()
   142→    now_dt = datetime.now(UTC)
   143→
   144→    # Collect all finding IDs referenced by the plan
   145→    referenced_ids: set[str] = set()
   146→    referenced_ids.update(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   147→    referenced_ids.update(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   148→    for override_id in plan.get("overrides", {}):
   149→        referenced_ids.add(override_id)
   150→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   151→        referenced_ids.update(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   152→
   153→    # Exclude already-superseded IDs and synthetic IDs (managed by stale_dimensions)
   154→    already_superseded = set(plan.get("superseded", {}).keys())
   155→    referenced_ids -= already_superseded
   156→    referenced_ids = {
   157→        fid for fid in referenced_ids
   158→        if not fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   159→        and fid != SYNTHESIS_ID
   160→    }
   161→
   162→    # Check each referenced ID
   163→    for fid in sorted(referenced_ids):
   164→        if not _is_finding_alive(state, fid):
   165→            if _supersede_id(plan, state, fid, now):
   166→                result.superseded.append(fid)
   167→                result.changes += 1
   168→
   169→    # Reconcile epic clusters: remove dead findings, delete empty epics
   170→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   171→    epic_names_to_delete: list[str] = []
   172→    for name, cluster in list(clusters.items()):
   173→        if not name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX):
   174→            continue
   175→        finding_ids = cluster.get("finding_ids", [])
   176→        alive_ids = [fid for fid in finding_ids if _is_finding_alive(state, fid)]
   177→        if alive_ids != finding_ids:
   178→            cluster["finding_ids"] = alive_ids
   179→            result.changes += 1
   180→        if not alive_ids:
   181→            epic_names_to_delete.append(name)
   182→    for name in epic_names_to_delete:
   183→        clusters.pop(name, None)
   184→        result.changes += 1
   185→
   186→    # Resurface stale temporary skips
   187→    scan_count = state.get("scan_count", 0)
   188→    from desloppify.engine._plan.operations import resurface_stale_skips
   189→
   190→    resurfaced = resurface_stale_skips(plan, scan_count)
   191→    if resurfaced:
   192→        result.resurfaced = resurfaced
   193→        result.changes += len(resurfaced)
   194→
   195→    # Prune old superseded entries
   196→    pruned = _prune_old_superseded(plan, now_dt)
   197→    result.pruned = pruned
   198→    result.changes += len(pruned)
   199→
   200→    # Log reconciliation if any changes were made
   201→    if result.changes > 0:
   202→        from desloppify.engine._plan.operations import append_log_entry
   203→
   204→        append_log_entry(
   205→            plan,
   206→            "reconcile",
   207→            finding_ids=result.superseded,
   208→            actor="system",
   209→            detail={
   210→                "superseded_count": len(result.superseded),
   211→                "pruned_count": len(result.pruned),
   212→                "resurfaced_count": len(result.resurfaced),
   213→            },
   214→        )
   215→
   216→    return result
   217→
   218→
   219→__all__ = [
   220→    "ReconcileResult",
   221→    "reconcile_plan_after_scan",
   222→]
   223→
